claims.text: Monolithic CoCrFeNi contains no incorporated lubricant phase.
Monolithic CoCrFeNi exhibits increased friction and wear, especially at high temperatures.
Oxidation and lack of lubrication cause the elevated-temperature friction and wear of monolithic CoCrFeNi.
Introducing approximately 5–10 vol% nano- or microscale h-BN can produce a dispersed composite microstructure in CoCrFeNi.
Dispersed h-BN particles act as a lubricious phase within the CoCrFeNi matrix.
The layered hexagonal structure of h-BN permits facile shear between basal planes.
Basal-plane shear in h-BN provides a self-lubricating effect.
h-BN is sufficiently thermally stable to remain an effective low-friction interface at elevated temperatures approaching 800 °C in air.
Dispersed h-BN forms a protective tribofilm during sliding.
The h-BN-derived tribofilm reduces wear even while the CoCrFeNi matrix undergoes oxidative changes.
Compared with monolithic CoCrFeNi, the h-BN composite will have a lower and more consistent coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
Compared with monolithic CoCrFeNi, the h-BN composite will have lower wear rates from room temperature to 800 °C.
The friction coefficient of the unmodified CoCrFeNi baseline increases at high temperature.
The wear performance of unmodified CoCrFeNi deteriorates at high temperature.
